correctness.rationale: The essential-norm tail formula is proved from finite-rank truncations and compactness of the adjoint on l1. Modulus domination is established for all powers of the complex interpolation F(z), giving the Calkin spectral-radius bound. Vesentini's subharmonicity theorem proves boundary spectral persistence, and openness of invertibility passes the result to z=1. The zero-radius case is handled separately.

value.rationale: Fredholm essential spectrum records failure of Fredholmness and is stable under compact perturbations. The inclusion gives a concrete persistence law for boundary Fredholm obstructions under positive domination at a fixed essential radius, without an ordinary spectral-radius growth hypothesis. This is more than a restatement of the ordinary-spectrum theorem because it works in the Calkin algebra through a c0-specific essential-norm identity.
